APPLY NOW
Steps on how to apply to Eastern Michigan University.
See below for step-by-step instructions on how to apply to EMU as an international applicant. Below the instructions we have also listed our Frequently Asked Questions.
Step 1: Submit your application
Expand dropdown
Apply here!
Please carefully follow the directions on the application portal. EMU will not have access to your application until the application fee is paid and the application is submitted.
Step 2: Submit Transcript/ Evaluations
Expand dropdown
Applicants with U.S. University transcripts:
Please have your current university send your official transcript directly to international_admissions@emich.edu or submit it via a secure transcript portal such as Parchment (sent institution-to-institution).
Applicants with post-secondary institutions outside of the U.S.:
If you attended any post secondary institutions outside of the U.S. you will be required to have all of your transcripts evaluated by one of the following services for a course-by-course evaluation. Acceptable evaluations must also include a copy of the original transcripts. Make sure that all of the evaluations are sent directly from the evaluation agency to international_admissions@emich.edu.
Educational Credential Evaluators (ECE)
Education Perspectives (EP)
The Evaluation Company (TEC)
World Education Service (WES)
These evaluation services are accredited through NACES. EMU will not accept evaluations from any other agency. Multiple evaluations will not be accepted, and EMU will only use the first submitted evaluation to make an application decision.
Step 3: Submit English Proficiency Test Scores
Expand dropdown
Submit your English proficiency test results through the testing agency to Eastern Michigan University. If you have taken the IELTS, TOEFL, or PTE you can email a copy of your official test results sheet to international_admissions@emich.edu and we add the test score to your application after verification. All other tests must be sent directly through the testing agency.
Accepted tests and minimum scores required:
TOEFL: 85
TOEFL Essentials: 9.5
IELTS: 6.5 (IELTS Indicator also accepted)
Pearson English Language Test (PTE): 70
Michigan English Test (MET): 60
Duolingo: 115
**The Graduate School accepts both MyBest scores and single-test-date TOEFL scores. Individual programs may choose not to accept MyBest scores and may require a higher level of English proficiency than required by the Graduate School.
Test scores are only valid for 2 years from the date of the application.

Step 4: Submit Remaining Application Documents
Expand dropdown
Each department may have specific requirements that you need to turn in before your application can be completed. Items like resumes, references, GRE/GMAT results, etc. Please follow the requirements listed on your application, or check out the programs catalog page for any additional requirements that need to be turned in.
Step 5: Begin I-20 Process
Expand dropdown
If you meet EMU's academic and English requirements for international students, you would be eligible to receive an I-20 from Eastern Michigan University. The Form I-20 is required to apply for an F-1 visa to study in the United States.
In order to process the I-20, you will be required to fill out the Financial Statement of Responsibility and Affidavit of Support Form [PDF] along with acceptable financial documents and a copy of your passport to international_admissions@emich.edu. Eastern Michigan University will only accept bank statements with liquid funds, acceptable bank statements must include the following information to be accepted:
Statement Date (No more than a year old from the time of program start date)
Name of the bank on letterhead or bank seal with signatures
Account Holder
Account Type (Checking, Savings, Current, Private, etc.)
Type of Currency
For Fixed/Term Deposits, statement must list maturity date (must be BEFORE the intended program start date) or that the funds are able to be withdrawn without penalty
All statements must be in English
Types of financial statements that will not be accepted:
Screenshots of account details will not be accepted
Any type of investment or investment account
Mutual Funds
Student Loans
Real Estate Holdings
Fixed/Term Deposits that mature AFTER the intended program start date
Any other type of account that is determined to not be liquid
EMU reserves the right to deny financial documents for any reason.
Applicants who are currently in the U.S. on an eligible visa that allows study (H-1B, H-4, L-1, L-2, etc.) will not need to apply for an I-20 unless you plan to change to an F-1 visa. Students who plan to study in another visa category will need to submit a copy of their visa along with their application materials before a decision can be made.
Frequently Asked Questions
How long will it take for admissions and the department to make a decision?
Expand dropdown
Once your application has been completed and ALL materials have been turned in we will send your application to the department for their review. Department review times may vary, so you should apply early.
Does EMU offer conditional admission?
Expand dropdown
No, EMU does not offer conditional admission.
What happens if I do not meet the English language requirements?
Expand dropdown
If your English score falls just below the minimum requirement, there may be an opportunity to go into the Graduate Studies ESL Pathway if you are academically admissible. If your score is too low, you can enter the Intensive English Program at EMU to work on your English.
Does EMU offer Graduate Assistantships?
Expand dropdown
Yes, occasionally the department may offer you a GA position as a part of your admissions offer, if not you can apply for any other available GA position on campus. See the Graduate Assistantships page for additional information.
Do grad students need to live in on campus housing?
Expand dropdown
No, international students are not required to live on campus.
I got a GA position, can you put that on my I-20?
Expand dropdown
If you have gotten a GA position and have not yet gone through the I-20 process you can submit the offer letter with you other financial documents.
If you have already received the I-20, you can submit the letter to our office and ask to have it added to your I-20. We will process a new I-20 with the GA information on it.
Should I contact Graduate Admissions, Grad School, International Admissions, or the program for my questions?
Expand dropdown
If your question pertains to your application you should always contact International Admissions at international_admissions@emich.edu. If you have specific questions about your intended program of study we suggest reaching out to the program directly.
Will I be able to work while I attend EMU?
Expand dropdown
Off campus employment is not allowed without authorization per F-1 visa regulations. You should talk to the Office of International Students and Scholars if you would like to explore internship opportunities.
On campus employment is allowed, and F-1 visa holders can work up to 20 hours a week.
